learning: Iteration 7 showed that an 8 mm footprint lowered the score (67.75 vs 70.83) with line losses unchanged, so the footprint question is closed in favour of 12 mm. Iteration 2 widened the span but was confounded with 16 mm footprints and a 0.5 kg body. This iteration isolates span at 12 mm. If line losses stay at 1.0 and the score falls, the next lever is wheel_track 0.14 m to damp turn rate.
notes: Iteration 8 package: the Builder's lateral span test (outer sensors ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing) on the iteration 6 best design, with sensor_size reverted to 0.012 m. The controller is identical to iteration 6, so the score change is attributable to span.
rationale: Iteration 6 (mass 0.4 kg, 12 mm footprints, span ±0.03 m, y 0.05 m, controller kp 3.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction) is the best design at 70.83. Its failure is unchanged: one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error 0.0641 and 0.0669 m. Steering oscillation is low (0.133 and 0.148), so the robot is not over-turning. Earlier single-variable tests have closed several levers: y 0.07 m did not remove the loss (iteration 3), body_length 0.12 m lowered the score (iteration 5), mass is at its 0.4 kg floor, and the 8 mm footprint lowered the score to 67.75 (iteration 7). The Builder's intent is to test lateral span alone at 12 mm, widening the outer sensors from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing. I adopt that geometry exactly as proposed: sensor_size 0.012, mass 0.4, body_length 0.16, y 0.05, wheel geometry unchanged. The controller is held at the iteration 6 values, including the same linear weights (+1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1), which still match the sensor order. Any gain change would confound the span test, and iteration 1 showed that raising gain did not help. Risk: at 0.02 m spacing the centre sensor is likely to read near 1 for small errors, which can flatten the signal near the centre. I will watch for this in the next race. Expected result, as a prediction only: line losses on the s-bend and slalom fall below 1.0 per run, max_error stays under 0.06 m for longer, and the score exceeds 70.83. If the score falls with progress unchanged, span is not the limit.
